header.sector: Power generation, grid and interconnection for AI datacenters
header.title: Vertically integrated energy-equipment firms win China AI datacenter power buildout

s01_bottom_line.text: Chinese industrial groups with roots in energy, construction and electrical equipment (Envision; the CATL/VNET/Zhongheng tie-up) are pivoting into AI datacenter infrastructure, pairing captive wind/solar/storage with in-hall power conversion. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩

The article suggests vertical integration gives integrated players more cost and schedule control and could matter more as power becomes harder to secure and the datacenter power system is redesigned.

If power access and the DC power-architecture shift become central to winning hyperscaler orders, integrated energy-equipment players could gain share and schedule/cost control, but the article says it is too early to confirm this and does not quantify any earnings effect.

items.text: Galaxy's wind farms have 420MW combined capacity, about 1.75x the 240MW datacenter load
In 2026 CATL became VNET's largest shareholder and announced a 49% stake in Zhongheng Electric's controlling shareholder
Envision's prefabricated substation takes under 3 months to connect vs about 6 months conventionally
Envision Group has more than 100GW of wind turbines installed worldwide
Envision built a 2GW off-grid wind/solar/storage system in Chifeng feeding a green ammonia plant
Envision's datacenter plans in Inner Mongolia add up to 3GW

s03_transmission.text: Access to power and redesigned grid-to-rack DC architecture are becoming part of what a datacenter developer sells, favoring integrated players.
Factory pre-configuration and prefab substations cut commissioning and deployment time (vs 3-6 months and ~6 months conventionally), giving cost and schedule control.
Would translate into datacenter and power-equipment orders/revenue for integrated players, but the article does not quantify any earnings effect and notes thin IRRs.
